name: Cholangiocarcinoma

ethnicAssociations: Higher incidence in Southeast Asian populations
Increased risk in patients with primary sclerosing cholangitis

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: No universally accepted formal criteria; diagnosis based on clinical, radiological, and histopathological findings

criteria.description: Imaging demonstrating bile duct mass or stricture consistent with malignancy
Histopathological confirmation of adenocarcinoma from bile duct biopsy or resected specimen
Laboratory evidence of cholestasis such as elevated alkaline phosphatase and gamma-glutamyl transferase

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Histopathological confirmation plus compatible imaging findings
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis often requires multidisciplinary evaluation including imaging, biopsy, and laboratory tests

laboratory: Elevated alkaline phosphatase and gamma-glutamyl transferase
imaging: CT or MRI demonstrating bile duct mass or stricture
ERCP with brush cytology or biopsy
other: Histopathology showing adenocarcinoma with glandular differentiation
Immunohistochemistry positive for CK7 and CK19

distinguishingFeatures: Chronic inflammatory strictures without mass lesion
Lack of malignant cells on biopsy
Mass centered in gallbladder rather than bile ducts
Obstructive jaundice with pancreatic duct involvement
Different tumor markers (e.g. CA 19-9 elevated but imaging distinct)

redFlags: Unexplained weight loss with cholestatic liver function tests
New onset pruritus with bile duct obstruction on imaging
references: Bridgewater J, Galle PR, Khan SA, et al. Guidelines for the diagnosis and management of intrahepatic cholangiocarcinoma. J Hepatol. 2014;60(6):1268-1289.
Razumilava N, Gores GJ. Cholangiocarcinoma. Lancet. 2014;383(9935):2168-2179.
